summary: Items in a container can be given a count above 99 (to max integer), and can crash the world
description: Using the following give command, item stacks can be given extremely high counts up to the java max integer. /give @s barrel[container=[{slot:0,item:{id:wooden_sword,count:2147483647}}]] Placing and then breaking the barrel will cause the stack to split into smaller stacks, spawn at least a few hundred million item entities, and crash the world. The split stacks seem to have random counts around 10 to 30, so it s slightly less than 2 billion entities spawned at once. Using commands to get an item with max_stack_size above 99 will detect and remove the invalid component, and setting the item count to below 1 will set it back to 1. Expected behavior would be for item count to be limited to the max_stack_size (or at least a hard coded max of 99).
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Open the chat and enter the command: `/give @s barrel[container=[{slot:0,item:{id:wooden_sword,count:2147483647}}]]`.
4. Place the barrel in the world.
5. Break the barrel after placing it.
6. Wait at least a few seconds and observe the game behavior.
7. Note that a large number of item entities spawn, causing the world to crash.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.20.5 Pre-Release 1, 1.20.5 Release Candidate 2, 1.20.6
Observed Behavior:
When using the command `/give @s barrel[container=[{slot:0,item:{id:wooden_sword,count:2147483647}}]]`, it is possible to create a barrel containing an item stack with a count exceeding the maximum allowable limit of 64 (the default stack size for most items) and even surpassing the Java maximum integer value of 2,147,483,647. Upon placing this barrel in the world and subsequently breaking it, the item stack splits into numerous smaller stacks. This results in the generation of a massive quantity of item entities, potentially spawning up to nearly 2 billion item entities at once, with individual stacks having random counts typically ranging from 10 to 30.

This behavior leads to significant performance issues, as the game struggles to handle the sheer number of item entities, ultimately causing the world to crash. Additionally, if commands are used to manipulate item counts in a way that exceeds the maximum stack size (e.g., using items with a max_stack_size greater than 99), the game will detect and remove the invalid stack component. If an item count is set below 1, it will automatically reset to 1, instead of allowing negative or zero counts.

The expected behavior in this scenario should enforce a strict limit on item counts to adhere to the max_stack_size of 64 (or at least a hard-coded maximum of 99), preventing the creation of stacks with invalid counts and avoiding the performance issues that arise from excessive item entity generation.
Expected Behavior: When using the /give command to place items in a barrel, the item count should be restricted to the maximum stack size of 64 for most items or 16 for certain others, ensuring that no item stack exceeds this limit. If an attempt is made to assign a count above the maximum stack size, the game should automatically correct the count to the highest valid value, preventing any world crashes or excessive item entity generation.
